subject: Biology
title: Allele Frequencies: Evolution's Scoreboard
description: A 60-second lesson on Allele Frequencies: Evolution's Scoreboard.

hook.text: Evolution isn't about individuals changing. It's about populations shifting—one allele at a time.

buildup.text: An allele is a version of a gene. Every population carries a mix of alleles at different frequencies.

discovery.text: Evolution occurs when allele frequencies change over generations—through selection, drift, or migration.

twist.text: A trait can be beneficial yet decrease in a small population—luck sometimes overrides fitness.

climax.text: Population genetics unifies Darwin's ideas with Mendel's genetics into the modern synthesis.

punchline.text: Evolution is a numbers game played with genes.

quiz.question: When does evolution occur in a population?
options: When allele frequencies change across generations

details.summary: Allele frequencies measure how common each gene variant is in a population. Evolution is fundamentally a change in allele frequencies over generations, driven by natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and gene flow. Tracking these frequencies reveals evolution in action.
details.whyItMatters: Allele frequencies make evolution measurable. Population geneticists track them to detect natural selection, predict disease risk in populations, and understand how species adapt, providing the quantitative backbone of evolutionary biology.
takeaways: Evolution is defined as a change in allele frequencies in a population
Selection increases frequencies of alleles that improve survival and reproduction
Genetic drift causes random frequency changes especially in small populations

faq.question: How do scientists measure allele frequencies?
faq.answer: By sampling individuals from a population and genotyping them at specific gene locations. The proportion of each allele version among all copies in the sample estimates its frequency. Large samples give more accurate estimates of the true population frequency.

faq.question: Can allele frequencies change without natural selection?
faq.answer: Yes. Genetic drift changes frequencies randomly, especially in small populations. Gene flow introduces alleles from other populations. Mutation creates new alleles. All four forces change allele frequencies independently of whether variants are beneficial.
